candidates.workingClaim: February 8, 1828: On February 8, 1828, the French writer Jules Verne was born in Nantes. His Extraordinary Journeys included Journey to the Centre of the Earth and Around the World in Eighty Days.
February 8, 1974: On February 8, 1974, the Skylab 4 crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean after 84 days in space, a new record for space endurance.
February 8, 1587: On February 8, 1587, Mary, Queen of Scots, the rival of Queen Elizabeth I of England, was beheaded at Fotheringhay Castle.
February 8, 1887: On February 8, 1887, the United States passed the Dawes General Allotment Act, providing for the distribution of Native American reservation land.
February 8, 1931: On February 8, 1931, the American actor James Dean was born.

February 9, 1996: On February 9, 1996, the German physicist Peter Armbruster and his team synthesized chemical element 112, a heavy element later named copernicium in honor of the astronomer Nicolaus Copernicus.
February 9, 1757: On February 9, 1757, the Treaty of Alinagar placed what is today Kolkata under British control, a prelude to the British seizure of Bengal.
February 9, 1940: On February 9, 1940, the South African novelist, critic and translator J.M. Coetzee was born. He won the 2003 Nobel Prize for Literature.
February 9, 1944: On February 9, 1944, the American writer Alice Walker was born. She is perhaps best known for her Pulitzer Prize-winning novel The Color Purple (1982).
February 9, 1984: On February 9, 1984, the Soviet leader Yury Andropov died, 15 months after succeeding Leonid Brezhnev. He was replaced by Konstantin Chernenko.
February 10, 1962: On February 10, 1962, Francis Gary Powers, the American U-2 pilot shot down over the Soviet Union in 1960, was exchanged for the jailed Soviet spy Rudolf Abel.
February 10, 1763: On February 10, 1763, the Treaty of Paris was signed, ending the territorial conflicts between France and Britain that had caused the Seven Years' War.
February 10, 1840: On February 10, 1840, Queen Victoria of Great Britain married Prince Albert.
February 10, 1898: On February 10, 1898, the poet and playwright Bertolt Brecht was born in Augsburg, Germany.
February 10, 1950: On February 10, 1950, the American swimmer Mark Spitz was born. He became the first athlete to win seven gold medals at a single Olympic Games.
February 11, 1990: On February 11, 1990, Nelson Mandela was released after 27 years in prison. He went on to negotiate with President F.W. de Klerk the end of apartheid in South Africa.
February 11, 1929: On February 11, 1929, Benito Mussolini of Italy and Pietro Gasparri of the Vatican signed the Lateran Treaty, recognizing papal sovereignty over Vatican City, an enclave in Rome.
February 11, 2011: On February 11, 2011, Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak stepped down after nearly 30 years in power, following the pro-democracy uprisings known as the Arab Spring.
February 11, 1847: On February 11, 1847, the inventor Thomas Edison was born in Ohio.
February 11, 1975: On February 11, 1975, Margaret Thatcher was elected leader of Britain's Conservative Party, replacing Edward Heath.
February 12, 1809: On February 12, 1809, Charles Darwin, who developed the theory of evolution by natural selection, was born in England. Abraham Lincoln was born on the same day.
February 12, 1809: On February 12, 1809, Abraham Lincoln was born. As the 16th president of the United States (1861-65), he preserved the Union during the American Civil War.
February 12, 1912: On February 12, 1912, Puyi, the last emperor of China, abdicated at the end of the Chinese Revolution.
February 12, 1818: On February 12, 1818, Chile formally declared its independence, exactly one year after revolutionary forces led by Jose de San Martin won a victory.
February 12, 1994: On February 12, 1994, thieves broke into the National Gallery in Oslo and stole a version of Edvard Munch's The Scream. The painting was recovered several months later.
February 13, 2000: On February 13, 2000, the last Peanuts comic strip was published, just hours after the death of its creator, Charles Schulz.
February 13, 2008: On February 13, 2008, Australian Prime Minister Kevin Rudd apologized to Australia's Aboriginal peoples for abuses they had suffered under earlier administrations.
February 13, 1960: On February 13, 1960, France detonated its first atomic bomb, in the Sahara desert.
February 13, 1883: On February 13, 1883, the German composer Richard Wagner died in Venice at age 69.
February 13, 1903: On February 13, 1903, the Belgian-French novelist Georges Simenon, creator of the Parisian police inspector Jules Maigret, was born in Liege, Belgium.

February 14, 1946: On February 14, 1946, the ENIAC (Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer), the first general-purpose electronic computer, was announced to the public. Built at the University of Pennsylvania, it used about 18,000 vacuum tubes and weighed 30 tons.
February 14, 1779: On February 14, 1779, the British explorer Captain James Cook was killed by Hawaiians at Kealakekua Bay.
February 14, 1912: On February 14, 1912, Arizona became a US state, the last of the 48 contiguous states to be admitted to the Union.
February 14, 2005: On February 14, 2005, Steve Chen, Chad Hurley and Jawed Karim registered YouTube, a website for sharing videos.
February 14, 2018: On February 14, 2018, South African President Jacob Zuma resigned amid scandals and corruption allegations.
